answer: Because the onyx lockup is checked by the reef escrow, the bridge audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. Running a large swarm thus freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants burn once per identity. The bond is locked for 26 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. That is 26 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
